headline: 661,654,158,300 distinct cases, re-enumerated 48 times.
what_the_big_number_is: 31,292,801,587,800 is a count of case EVALUATIONS, not of cases. The overnight loop runs the same five deterministic lattice sweeps over and over until a stop hour and adds the case count every pass. There is no random number generator in any of the five sweeps - a search for random, seed, choice or sample returns nothing - so they are fixed mixed-radix lattices, and pass 2 evaluates the identical set of points as pass 1. Repetition is a soak test. It is not coverage, and quoting it as a case count overstates what was examined by a factor of 48.

the_two_earlier_figures_and_what_each_go.17391591847800: The first published figure. Wrong twice over: it is an evaluation count presented as a case count, AND it was missing one sweep entirely. The counter read the key 'cases' from each sweep's result file and one sweep writes 'space' and 'evaluated' instead. A missing key was answered with a number, 0, which then went into a total. That sweep ran 47 times, re-verified card against processor every time, recorded 0 differ every time, and was logged as a success contributing nothing.
the_two_earlier_figures_and_what_each_go.31292801587800: The correction to the missing key. It fixed the omission and left the deeper error in place: still an evaluation count published as though it were coverage. That is the figure this file replaces.

how_the_missing_key_was_found: The per-pass figure was exactly the sum of four of the five sweeps while the failure count read zero. Those two facts cannot both be innocent.
how_the_repetition_was_found: The loop's own log prints the five per-sweep counts every pass, identical to the last digit 48 times. A sweep returning the same count on every pass over a lattice with no RNG is enumerating the same points.
verification_unaffected: Every pass re-verified the card against the processor before reporting and recorded 0 differ. Nothing here relaxes a check. What changes is only what the number may be called.
not_claimed: A distinct-case count is a count of points examined. It is not evidence that the points were the right ones, nor that the limits they were compared against have a source. Two of the four limits this estate measures against do not.
anonymised: No project, site, client, maker or model anywhere.
